capabilities: Translate selected text in Markdown editors, reading views and PDFs
Look up English words with pronunciation, parts of speech and definitions
Translate full PDFs into bilingual Markdown with optional comparison HTML
Configure built-in translation services and OpenAI-compatible model profiles
Style popup and sidebar typography with fonts, sizes and spacing
disambiguation: Despite the name, it is not limited to short snippets; it also translates whole PDFs into Markdown and comparison HTML files.
extras: Desktop-only. The author has only reviewed Chinese and English language directions; other languages are untested by native speakers. Credentials are stored in plaintext in data.json unless Secure mode moves them to Obsidian Keychain, and exported configuration JSON contains API keys.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to translate selected text or whole PDFs, so reading foreign-language notes and papers means switching to an outside app.

relations.evidence: Parts of the translation-provider request logic were adapted from Translate for Zotero
The PDF integration design was informed by PDF++

requires.name: API key for DeepL or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
OpenAI-compatible LLM provider for full-PDF translation

summary: Desktop-only translator that translates selected text in editors, reading views and PDFs, looks up English words, and converts full PDFs to bilingual Markdown.
